Contrived (no tool writes this shape and an impostor needs a CA-issued leaf on the probe port), but E4/E5 do not lower the derived HIGH. The Architect settled the design question on evidence, not taste: a throwaway differential harness outside the repo compared the scanner with OpenSSL 3.6.1's reader on 10,015 layouts (15 fixed, 10,000 random from 26 fragment kinds; the server boots on 1,940 of them): the old scanner disagreed on 71, the guarded scanner on 0 (0 widenings, 578 agreements, the rest fail closed), so keeping the scanner and adding a guard stands, and anchoring through OpenSSL's own reader was rejected as new surface (BIO/X509 ownership, re-encoding) that would also flip the alias-label contract the docs and tests pin. Fixed in 2551fb1e1: after the marker is found, a BEGIN that is not at the start of a line (an optional UTF-8 BOM at byte 3 is allowed) returns empty and the doc comment states the OpenSSL rule; pure cases (mid-line, indented, BOM at 3, BOM elsewhere, double BOM, CRLF) plus a live sibling-refusal case on the reported layout; mutation probes (guard removed, BOM allowance removed, BOM allowance widened to b<=3) are each red, and the reported layout now exits 1 with one 'SSL certificate loading failed' line.

trigger: one text in 80M from a PEM-structure differential (the scanner's block read the way httplib's load_ca_pem reads it, against the block the OpenSSL 3.6.1 file reader takes as the leaf) where the decoded bytes differ: a BOM-prefixed BEGIN line padded with spaces and holding a NUL, with base64 text after the NUL on the same physical line
summary: Residual of the first-PEM anchor guard (first_pem_certificate, added in b6c6c2898, refined at de495f580 and 2551fb1e1), not introduced by the line-start fix. The reporter verified it at the PEM-reader layer only (not end to end with real certificates, not root-caused) and held it at derived HIGH pending triage. Root cause, verified by the architect: the 876-byte sample is a UTF-8 BOM, the BEGIN marker, 226 spaces, a NUL at byte 256 and 64 base64 characters on one 321-byte first line; OpenSSL reads lines in 254-byte chunks; the BOM shifts the chunk boundary by 3 bytes between the server's whole-file read and the scanner's BOM-less block; the file reader (fgets + strlen) cuts a chunk at a NUL while the memory reader httplib uses counts bytes, so the server's first block decodes to 69 bytes and the probe's to 117.
